evidence.note: Branch frozen: no source, test, doc or config file in the repository was created, edited or deleted. The only file written is this result JSON. All experiments ran against a full copy of the tree in the session scratchpad; no binary was built into the repository.

No shard result exists yet for plan 232e5c0c067629e5 (the results directory holds only earlier plans' shard-00..shard-3f files), so this review was conducted directly against the seams rather than by aggregating shard inputs. Read the full text of internal/fsm/judge/diffselect.go, internal/fsm/sandbox/sandbox.go, internal/fsm/cli/escalation.go, internal/fsm/kind/kind.go's diff, internal/fsm/machine/diff.go, internal/fsm/run/event.go + types.go, internal/jsonl/jsonl.go, internal/status/status.go, internal/fsm/judge/prompts.go, plus every doc and spec hunk in the range.

Findings 1 and 2 were proved empirically, not inferred. Copied the tree to the scratchpad, added two throwaway probe tests to internal/fsm/cli that reuse the real escalationHarness (real git repo, real diff, real sandbox.Materialize, only the codex subprocess faked), ran them, then deleted the probes. Probe 1: a repo file whose bytes are "package f

func Added() {}
" is materialized into the sandbox as "package f

func Added() {}" - the trailing newline is gone. Probe 2: a repo file whose bytes are "

package f

func Added() {}
" is materialized as "package f

func Added() {}", moving `func Added` from line 5 in the repository to line 3 in the tree the escalating judge reads. Both probes also counted 591 leftover mrv-evidence-* directories in $TMPDIR on this machine.
Finding 3 was established by enumerating every bufio.NewScanner and jsonl.NewScanner call site in internal/ and cmd/ and then checking, per call site, whether the file it scans is a .jsonl file.
Read-only sanity gates over the scratchpad copy: `gofmt -l ./internal ./cmd` empty and `go vet ./...` clean at the reviewed head.

findings.note:
The evidence sandbox does not contain the code it claims to contain: every materialized file is whitespace-trimmed, so it matches neither revision and its line numbers shift. internal/fsm/cli/escalation.go:99-108 builds the sandbox.ShowFunc out of `c.git(root, "show", "--no-ext-diff", rev+":"+path)` and returns `[]byte(out)`, but `c.git` at internal/fsm/cli/wiring.go:38-41 is `strings.TrimSpace(string(out))` - a helper written for short git outputs (SHAs, ref names, worktree lines), never for file content. sandbox.Materialize then writes those trimmed bytes and content-addresses them into Tree.TreeHash. Two consequences, both proved by running the real provider in the scratchpad copy: (a) every file in head/ and base/ loses its trailing newline, and a file with leading blank lines loses those too - a file that is "

package f

func Added() {}
" in the repository becomes "package f

func Added() {}" in the sandbox, moving `func Added` from line 5 to line 3; (b) because run.Finding carries File and Line taken from the diff's post-image numbering, the escalating judge is pointed at the wrong line of a file whose content is not either revision's. That defeats the purpose of the arm: escalation exists specifically to rescue findings the excerpt arm got wrong, and it is fed misaligned evidence. It also falsifies two claims in other shards - internal/fsm/sandbox/sandbox.go:9-10 ("content-addressing the tree restores it") and CHANGELOG.md:30-32 ("content-addresses it with a tree hash so a verdict stays replayable") - since the hash addresses a tree that reproduces no commit. Nothing catches it: internal/fsm/cli/escalation_test.go:81-91 asserts only os.Stat existence of head/f.go, base/f.go and head/'new file.go', never a byte of content, and internal/fsm/sandbox/sandbox_test.go drives Materialize through a fake ShowFunc that returns exact bytes, so the corruption lives entirely in the seam between the two packages. Fix: give escalation.go a raw git accessor (c.deps.Exec directly, untrimmed) instead of reusing c.git, and add a content-equality assertion to escalation_test.go for both a file with a trailing newline and a file with leading blank lines.

findings.note: The evidence sandbox is created per run and never deleted. internal/fsm/cli/escalation.go:37 calls c.deps.TempDir("mrv-evidence-"), bound to os.MkdirTemp at internal/fsm/cli/deps.go:69; `grep -rn RemoveAll` over internal/ shows no cleanup anywhere for that directory, while internal/fsm/gate/git.go:255 is this codebase's own convention for exactly this pattern (`defer func() { _ = os.RemoveAll(dir) }()`). The sandbox is a full copy of every changed path at BOTH revisions, plus every path any finding names, written mode 0444 - on this branch that is 538 files per escalating run. Measured on the reviewing machine: 591 `mrv-evidence-*` directories already sitting in $TMPDIR, i.e. the leak is not hypothetical, it is already happening from the new test suite. Escalation is on by default, so every unattended `fsm advance` that rejects a cross-file candidate adds another copy. Nothing in CHANGELOG.md, docs/fsm/driving-a-workflow.md or skills/fsm/SKILL.md says the tree is retained, so this is not a documented deliberate choice. The judge call has already returned by the time escalationFor's caller is done with the tree, so a `defer`-style removal after the executor finishes is safe; if retention is wanted for replay it needs to be a stated contract with a location and a retention rule, not an unbounded /tmp leak.

findings.note: internal/jsonl's package doc claims a guarantee it does not deliver, and the refactor stopped at five of nine call sites. jsonl.go:1-2 reads 'Package jsonl centralises the line cap shared by every reader of the repository's .jsonl files (findings.jsonl, runs.jsonl, review logs, run chains).' Five readers were converted: internal/state/state.go:63, internal/fsm/record/record.go:155, internal/runchain/runchain.go:112, internal/findings/findings.go:486, internal/reviewlog/reviewlog.go:287. Four readers of .jsonl files were not, and still run bufio's 64 KiB default: internal/sessionhistory/sessionhistory.go:226 (reads ~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl and ~/.codex/history.jsonl transcripts, where lines over 64 KiB are routine - a single assistant turn with a large tool result exceeds it), internal/knowledge/knowledge.go:73 (every *.jsonl under the knowledge directory), internal/epicsource/epicsource.go:86 and internal/tasksource/tasksource.go:63 (both .beads/issues.jsonl). All four check scanner.Err(), so the failure mode is a hard 'bufio.Scanner: token too long' that aborts the whole file - post-merge learning or epic/task resolution failing outright on input another component wrote successfully, which is precisely the failure jsonl.go's own doc comment describes and claims to have eliminated. This is the pattern this branch has shipped repeatedly: one semantic change applied to most, not all, of its call sites. It is invisible per shard because jsonl.go is in shard-5 while none of the four unconverted files appear in the diff at all.

findings.note: Untrusted finding text selects which repository files are copied into the judge's sandbox, contradicting two doc claims, and one malformed path in that text disables escalation for the rest of the run. internal/fsm/judge/diffselect.go:285-288 states the containment argument for the whole design: 'The finding text is untrusted reviewer output, so it selects which of OUR OWN hunks to show and nothing more.' AllReferencedPaths (diffselect.go:361-377) deliberately drops the diff filter, and internal/fsm/cli/escalation.go:61-77 (referencedByFindings) feeds its output straight into sandbox.Materialize's path list - so the untrusted text does select arbitrary repository paths at head, well beyond 'our own hunks'. CHANGELOG.md:30-32 makes the same overstatement from the other side: the sandbox is 'every changed path at base and head, mode 0444, nothing else', when it is in fact the changed set PLUS up to maxReferencedFiles paths per finding that the branch never touched. Path containment itself holds (sandbox.go:54-57 refuses anything that cleans to '..' or is absolute), but the refusal is a hard error: Materialize returns it, escalationFor propagates it, and adjudicateExec.resolve caches it in resolveErr under sync.Once (kind.go:558-564), so a single finding whose prose contains a relative path like '../../internal/x.go' - which referencedPath at diffselect.go:295 matches, since '.' and '-' are in its character class - turns every subsequent cross-file rejection in that run into checked_but_unverified. Untrusted reviewer prose should not be able to switch the second-opinion arm off for a whole run; filter the referenced paths for containment before Materialize sees them (silently dropping the ones that escape) rather than letting one bad token become a run-wide error.

findings.note: Report.EvidenceMismatch cannot count the divergence the docs sell it for. internal/fsm/machine/diff.go:49-52: compare() returns early whenever row.A or row.B is nil, so EvidenceSame is computed and EvidenceMismatch incremented only for two-sided rows. But the escalated call and the primary call it follows are issued with the SAME judge.Request Input (kind.go:529 and :588 both build ContextForClaim over the same candidate), and InputHash is computed from Input alone (judge.go:535, prompts.go:183) - the model is not in it. So an escalating run emits two llm_call rows with identical (node, iter, kind, input_hash) where a --no-escalate run emits one; the second is disambiguated only by the unexported occurrence counter and pairs with nothing on the other side. The realistic comparison - a run with escalation against the same run with --no-escalate, which is precisely what an operator would diff - therefore reports evidence_mismatch: 0. skills/fsm/SKILL.md:42, docs/fsm/driving-a-workflow.md:117-119 and docs/specs/2026-08-27-metareview-0.9.0-fsm-cli.md:123-125 all present evidence_mismatch as the signal for exactly that case. Same=false still surfaces the row, so this is a reporting gap rather than a silent pass, but the documented counter does not mean what three documents say it means.

findings.note: The two new path predicates that gate the whole feature are unnormalized string heuristics with no shared definition and no observability. (a) internal/fsm/kind/kind.go:517-527 decides 'no evidence, no question' by exact string equality between cand.File and git's post-image path (judge.DiffHasFile -> parseUnifiedDiff -> postImagePathFromHeader). A discover node that emits './internal/x.go', 'a/internal/x.go', a leading-slash path, or a pre-rename path silently converts a judgeable finding into an unjudged unverified_no_evidence for a human; nothing normalizes the candidate's file, and no counter or warning records how often the guard fires, so a systematic mismatch between a reviewer's path convention and git's would look exactly like a run where nothing was checkable. (b) internal/fsm/judge/diffselect.go:302's rootFile regex `\b[A-Za-z0-9_-]{2,}\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,5}\b` matches version strings: 'metareview 0.10.0' yields '10.0', and MentionsOtherFiles (kind.go:571) is deliberately NOT diff-filtered, so a finding that names no file at all triggers a sandbox materialization and a second full judge call. Both predicates are consumed from packages other than the one that defines them (kind consumes judge; cli consumes judge), which is why neither shard sees the combination. A single normalization helper in judge, applied to cand.File before DiffHasFile and to namedPaths' output, plus a run-level count of unverified_no_evidence and of escalations triggered, would make both observable.
